title: Granite vs. Marble: An Architectural Comparison
summary: Understanding the fundamental differences in geological hardness, porosity, maintenance, and ideal applications between igneous granite and metamorphic marble.

comparisonTable.granite: Igneous rock formed by cooling molten magma under extreme pressure
comparisonTable.marble: Metamorphic rock formed when limestone recrystallizes under tectonic heat

comparisonTable.granite: 6 to 7 (Extremely hard & scratch resistant)
comparisonTable.marble: 3 to 4 (Softer, susceptible to scratches from cutlery)

comparisonTable.granite: Low porosity; highly resistant to lemon, vinegar and cooking oils
comparisonTable.marble: Porous & calcium-rich; prone to acid etching if unsealed

comparisonTable.granite: Granular, crystalline speckled or flowing ribbon motion
comparisonTable.marble: Soft, expressive veining, feathery clouds, luminous depth

comparisonTable.granite: Heavy-duty kitchen counters, stairs, exterior paving, vanity tops
comparisonTable.marble: Living room flooring, master bathrooms, fireplace surrounds, feature walls

recommendation: For active family kitchens with frequent heavy cooking, granite offers near-indestructible durability. For opulent living room flooring and luxury spa bathrooms, marble provides unmatched natural radiance and cool sophistication.

title: Natural Granite vs. Engineered Quartz
summary: Natural earth-hewn stone versus advanced engineered quartz crystals. How to choose based on stain resistance, heat tolerance, and aesthetic uniformity.

comparisonTable.granite: 100% natural quarried stone slab
High when properly sealed once every 12-18 months
comparisonTable.quartz: Exceptional; 100% non-porous with zero sealing required

comparisonTable.granite: Exceptional; can handle hot pans directly from stove
comparisonTable.quartz: Moderate; hot pans can cause resin discoloration (trivet recommended)

comparisonTable.granite: Every slab is unique with natural variations & mineral marks
comparisonTable.quartz: Predictable, controlled veining with uniform color matching

comparisonTable.granite: Periodic sealing; pH-neutral stone cleaner
comparisonTable.quartz: Virtually zero maintenance; soapy water wash

recommendation: Choose natural granite if you value 100% natural authenticity, unique mineral variation, and superior heat resistance. Choose engineered quartz if you want consistent veining (like Italian Calacatta) with zero periodic sealing.

title: Understanding Modern Tile Types
summary: A guide through Vitrified, Glazed Vitrified (GVT), Full Body Vitrified, and Large-Format Porcelain Slabs for Kolhapur homes and commercial developments.

comparisonTable.granite: Two-layer porcelain with 3-4mm design layer
comparisonTable.marble: High abrasion resistance; ideal for heavy residential foot traffic

comparisonTable.granite: High-definition digital printed glaze on vitrified base
comparisonTable.marble: Endless design variety (marble, wood, cement patterns) with polished or matte tops

comparisonTable.granite: Uniform color throughout the entire tile thickness
comparisonTable.marble: Scratch proof and color permanent; ideal for commercial atriums and shops

comparisonTable.granite: Continuous porcelain slabs with minimal joints
comparisonTable.marble: Replaces natural marble slabs on feature walls and expansive floors

recommendation: For living spaces, Large-Format GVT slabs reduce joint lines and simulate natural marble. For bathrooms and wet balconies, opt for matte or rustic slip-resistant surfaces.

title: Surface Finishes: Polished vs. Matte vs. Leathered
summary: How different surface treatments alter stone aesthetics, light reflection, slip resistance, and tactile sensation.

comparisonTable.granite: High-gloss reflective sheen buffed with fine diamond abrasives
comparisonTable.marble: Enhances stone color depth; reflects light; best for indoor walls & low-slip floors

comparisonTable.granite: Smooth, flat surface with zero glossy glare
comparisonTable.marble: Velvety touch; hides micro-scratches; excellent for modern architectural sanctuaries

comparisonTable.granite: Textured, tactile rippled finish that follows stone geology
comparisonTable.marble: Hides fingerprints and water spots; warm organic touch for granite counters

comparisonTable.granite: High-heat thermal treatment leaving rough, crystalline texture
comparisonTable.marble: Superior anti-slip traction for exterior ramps, pool surrounds and landscape steps

recommendation: Polished finishes maximize light and luxury in living rooms. Leathered and honed finishes are trending for contemporary kitchen countertops because they hide fingerprints and offer a soft, tactile experience.

title: Natural Stone Care & Longevity Guide
summary: Simple daily practices, cleaning dos and don'ts, and sealing schedules to preserve your stone for generations.

comparisonTable.granite: Microfiber mop or warm water with mild pH-neutral soap
comparisonTable.marble: Avoid acidic toilet cleaners, vinegar, lemon juice, or abrasive scouring pads

comparisonTable.granite: Blot spills immediately with a soft cloth rather than wiping across
comparisonTable.marble: Pay special attention to turmeric, coffee, wine, and tomato purees on marble

comparisonTable.granite: Apply penetrating solvent-based sealer once every 12 to 24 months
comparisonTable.marble: Check with water drop test: if water darkens the stone in 5 mins, re-sealing is due

recommendation: Never use harsh bathroom acid cleaners on natural marble or polished granite. A simple warm water wash with a pH-neutral cleaner keeps stone pristine for decades.

title: Selecting the Right Kitchen Countertop
summary: Balancing cooking habits, color schemes, sink integration, and edge profiling for Indian kitchen requirements.

comparisonTable.granite: High exposure to turmeric, tamarind, hot cookware and rolling pins (belan)
comparisonTable.marble: Black Galaxy, Absolute Black, or Quartz are top recommendations

comparisonTable.granite: Full Bullnose, Half Bullnose, Pencil Chamfer, or Mitered Waterfall
comparisonTable.marble: Chamfer and full bullnose prevent chipping along sink cutouts

comparisonTable.granite: Provide solid plywood carcass or stone support battens
comparisonTable.marble: Prevents deflection under heavy granite slab weight (approx 45-55 kg/m²)

recommendation: For heavy daily cooking, Absolute Black Granite or Black Galaxy Granite remains the undisputed champion. For light, modern Scandinavian open kitchens, Calacatta Quartz offers effortless luxury.

title: Stone Thickness & Installation Considerations
summary: 18mm vs. 20mm standards, leveling mortars, expansion joints, and edge reinforcement guidelines.

comparisonTable.granite: Granite: 18mm & 20mm calibrated slabs
comparisonTable.marble: Marble: 18mm standard gangsaw cut slabs

comparisonTable.granite: Quartz: 15mm & 20mm engineered panels
comparisonTable.marble: Vitrified: 9mm to 12mm thickness

comparisonTable.granite: Polymer-modified stone adhesive or 1:4 cement-sand dry bed with slurry
comparisonTable.marble: Ensures complete solid bedding without hollow pockets underneath

comparisonTable.granite: Provide 2mm to 3mm spacers on large tile floors
comparisonTable.marble: Allows thermal movement and prevents tenting or cracking over time

recommendation: Always inspect full slabs in person at our Shiroli showroom to verify color consistency and thickness calibration before dry-laying on site.
